title: Lovepreet Singh Wins Silver, Seema Bags Bronze as India Adds to CWG Tally
excerpt: Weightlifter Lovepreet Singh missed gold by just 1kg in the men's +110kg final, while discus thrower Seema Kaliramna earned India's fourth bronze at Glasgow 2026.
body:
• Lovepreet Singh lifted 388kg to claim silver in men's +110kg weightlifting, losing gold to New Zealand's David Liti by just 1kg.
  • Seema Kaliramna threw 58.65m to win bronze in women's discus throw, with teammate Nidhi Rani finishing fourth at 57.10m.
  • India's weightlifting team has now won eight medals in Glasgow, including one gold and six silver.
  • India sits 10th on the medal table with 3 gold, 10 silver, and 4 bronze after Day 8 of competition.

India added two more medals to its Commonwealth Games haul on Day 8 in Glasgow, with weightlifter Lovepreet Singh claiming silver and discus thrower Seema Kaliramna securing bronze in their respective finals on Thursday.

Lovepreet Falls 1kg Short of Gold

Lovepreet Singh delivered a commanding performance in the men's +110kg weightlifting final at the SEC Centre, only to be denied gold by the slimmest of margins. The 28-year-old Indian Navy sailor lifted a total of 388kg — 176kg in the snatch and 212kg in the clean and jerk — finishing just 1kg behind New Zealand's David Liti, who totalled 389kg.

Lovepreet dominated the snatch phase, clearing 168kg, 173kg, and 176kg in successive attempts to set a new Commonwealth Games record and lead the field heading into the clean and jerk. He opened strongly with 205kg and followed up with 212kg, but his ambitious third attempt at 217kg proved too much, and the lift failed.

"Seema has never looked for shortcuts. Whether it was returning after motherhood or balancing her PhD alongside training, she has approached everything with discipline and consistency."

— Ravinder Kaliramna, Coach and Husband

That left the door open for Liti, who had trailed after the snatch with 166kg. The New Zealander produced a decisive 223kg clean and jerk — the heaviest of the competition — to edge past Lovepreet by the narrowest possible margin. England's Andrew Griffiths took bronze with 356kg.

The silver marks an improvement on Lovepreet's bronze from the 2022 Birmingham Games, where he competed in the 109kg category. Born in Bal Sachandar village near Amritsar, Punjab, he began weightlifting at 13 before joining the Indian Navy in 2015 and has steadily risen through the heavyweight ranks.

Seema Kaliramna Earns Discus Bronze

At the Scotstoun Stadium, Seema Kaliramna gave India another reason to celebrate with a bronze medal in the women's discus throw. The 30-year-old achieved her best throw of 58.65m in the third round to secure the podium finish in what has been the strongest season of her career.

Jamaica's Samantha Hall won gold with a throw of 61.66m, while Canada's Julia Tunks took silver at 60.67m. India's Nidhi Rani narrowly missed a second Indian medal, finishing fourth with 57.10m.

Seema's journey to the podium has been unconventional. A mother who returned to competitive athletics while simultaneously pursuing a PhD, she has credited patience and consistency for her resurgence. Her husband and coach, Ravinder Kaliramna, has worked with her on refining technical details that paid dividends in Glasgow.

India's Medal Position

With Lovepreet's silver and Seema's bronze, India now has 17 medals in total — 3 gold, 10 silver, and 4 bronze — but sits 10th in the overall standings, behind nations with more gold medals. Australia leads the table with 51 gold and 110 total medals, followed by England (15 gold, 65 total) and Canada (15 gold, 45 total).

India's weightlifting contingent has been the standout, producing eight medals including Mirabai Chanu's gold in the women's 48kg and six silver medals across various weight classes. On the athletics track, Seema's bronze adds to silver medals won by Murali Sreeshankar (long jump), Gulveer Singh (10,000m), and Sarvesh Kushare (high jump).

What's Next for India

India's campaign enters its final stretch with Neeraj Chopra set to compete in the javelin throw qualifying round on Thursday, carrying enormous expectations. Athletics events continue to offer medal opportunities across track and field disciplines, while the wrestling and boxing competitions — traditionally strong suits for India — are yet to reach their medal stages. With five days of competition remaining, India will look to convert its silver-heavy tally into gold to climb higher on the medal table.
